_README: Human-reviewed baseline of sensitive-pattern scrub hits in the public export.
Consumed by scripts/check_public_export_redactions.py, which is the gate on
the unattended weekly refresh (.github/workflows/public-explorer-refresh.yml).
A scrub hit whose (record_type, record_id, field, pattern) key appears below
has been looked at by a person and judged correct. Any hit NOT listed here
fails the scheduled run, which then publishes nothing and asks for review.
WHAT THIS GATE IS ACTUALLY FOR -- read this before assuming it stops leaks.
It does not, because nothing needs it to: the scrub in export_public_explorer.py
DROPS the whole field on any match, unconditionally, listed here or not. A new
hit therefore cannot publish a leak even if this file is empty and the gate is
asleep. What unattended publishing actually loses is the HUMAN, and with them
two things the scrub cannot do for itself:
1. OVER-REDACTION going unnoticed -- the real hazard. The scrub is deliberately
blunt (one match kills the entire field), so a legitimate result summary that
happens to contain a hostname vanishes from the public site silently. Nothing
errors. The page just quietly has less science on it than it should.
2. Nobody fixing the SOURCE. A machine identity in an evidence_direction_note is
a defect in the note, and the scrub hides it well enough that it survives.
So the review question for each entry is NOT 'is dropping this safe?' (always yes)
but 'should this field have been publishable, and is the source worth fixing?'.
KEYED ON (record_type, record_id, field, pattern), DELIBERATELY NOT ON `matched`.
The matched substring is recorded for the reviewer but excluded from the key: if
an already-approved note is edited and trips the SAME pattern on a different host,
the field is dropped either way, so re-review buys nothing and the churn would
train people to rubber-stamp. A hit on a NEW record is the reviewable event.
TO APPROVE new hits after reviewing them:
python3 scripts/check_public_export_redactions.py --update --reviewed-by <name>
then replace each generated `note` placeholder with the actual finding.
Entries that no longer fire are reported as stale but never fail the run --
a fixed source is good news. Prune them when convenient.
